subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps

Hi Jordan —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our call plus proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the performance SLOs you asked about:

Summary of Acme requirements (from call)
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): target <= 120ms p95 for production traffic (goal: 100ms).
- Streaming: client needs streaming responses over SSE (preferred) or WebSocket as fallback.
- Chunk cadence: prefer first partial chunk within the TTFT window and subsequent chunks at ~150–300ms cadence for conversational UX.
- Throughput / concurrency: baseline 120 qps average, burst up to 600 qps; expected concurrency on a single endpoint ~200 concurrent model sessions.
- Payloads: median prompt length ~120 tokens, 95th ~600 tokens.

What Redwood can deliver / next steps
1) PoC benchmark: run a 24–48 hour synthetic test with your sample traffic (we’ll use your input distribution) to validate TTFT and streaming cadence at target concurrency.
2) SLO matrix & test plan: attached is a draft SLO matrix and a proposed TTFT test plan (slo-matrix.xlsx, ttft-test-plan.md). Please confirm these reflect your targets.
3) Data we need from you: 24–72h request traces (anonymized) or a representative sample of prompts, and an indication of peak windows (timezone-aware).
4) Timeline: if we get test data by next Tue (Mar 3), we can kick off a PoC test the week of Mar 9 and deliver a results deck by Mar 16.

Technical notes (quick)
- We’ll benchmark both SSE and WebSocket streaming paths; TTFT differences are usually in the 10–30ms range depending on client handshake.
- We recommend warm KV cache priming for steady-state TTFT; cold-start cases will be covered in the test plan.
- For chunk cadence we’ll tune the model generation chunking (token batch size) and the runtime flush interval to match your UX needs.

Can you confirm the targets above and share the sample traces (S3 link or Drive) and a good contact on your engineering side? Once we have that I’ll loop in Marissa for the test setup and Dev for infra specifics.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: slo-matrix.xlsx, ttft-test-plan.md

From: Jordan Mills <jordan@acme-retail.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps

Thanks, Aditya — this is exactly the right level of detail. Confirming from our side:
- TTFT target: p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 250ms (we want both numbers in the report).
- Streaming: SSE preferred (web clients), WebSocket for our mobile apps.
- Cadence: aim for first chunk within TTFT and then ~200ms average cadence thereafter — tolerance +/- 100ms.
- Traffic: our ops team will extract a 72-hour anonymized sample (JSON lines) and share an S3 presigned link. Expect that by COB Mon, Mar 2.

One more Q: we occasionally see prompt spikes (very long prompts ~2k tokens) — will those be included in the PoC or excluded? We’d like the PoC to focus on realistic distribution but also highlight how extremes affect TTFT.

Jordan
Engineering Manager, Platform
Acme Retail
jordan@acme-retail.com

Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 08:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps

Hi Jordan — looping in the tech team to answer the prompt-spike question and give execution details for the PoC. Quick notes:

On prompt spikes:
- We will include the 2k-token extremes in a separate test bucket. The PoC will run two profiles: (A) realistic distribution (0–600 tokens, as you described) and (B) extremes (600–2k tokens) so you can see tail behavior.

PoC plan (technical)
- Ingress: we’ll replay your anonymized sample traffic through our isolated PoC cluster (VPC).
- Measurement points: we’ll capture TTFT at the API gateway, the model runtime first-token emission, and client-delivery time for SSE/WebSocket.
- Streaming cadence: measurement will include inter-chunk latency histogram (we instrument flush intervals; target mean ~200ms).
- Concurrency load: we’ll sweep 50 -> 600 concurrent sessions to map TTFT degradation curves.
- Artifacts: results deck, per-endpoint SLO table, raw latency histograms, and a small reproducer script.

Dev note (Cc): can you confirm we have access to a test VPC endpoint and that the S3 sample will be reachable from our PoC infra? Also flag any IP allowlist needs.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachments referenced: test harness repo link (will share after kickoff)
